content.title: The Masters 2026: TV coverage, Augusta National schedule, Featured Groups, Amen Corner stream and how to watch or stream on Sky Sports
content.text:
A thrilling Sunday is expected at The Masters, with extended coverage from the final round exclusively live on Sky Sports Golf.

Rory McIlroy made a remarkable start to the defence of his title, establishing a record lead at the halfway stage at Augusta National as he seeks to become the first back-to-back winner since Tiger Woods.

He stuttered in his third-round 73, slipping back into a share of the lead alongside Cameron Young, although remains in pole position to claim a sixth major title.

  • Rory McIlroy races into historic Masters lead
  • Rory McIlroy's Grand Slam success: Essential reading
  • Get Sky Sports or stream golf with no contract

Sam Burns holds third spot ahead of Shane Lowry, who posted a hole-in-one during Saturday's third round, with Jason Day, Justin Rose and Scottie Scheffler among those still in the running to win the Green Jacket.

Sky Sports continues to be the home of The Masters in the UK and Ireland, with more full action from tournament days than ever before and there has been live coverage every day this week.

Here's a closer look at the key TV and streaming times and ways to follow all the action…

When is The Masters live on Sky Sports Golf?

Live coverage was available on all three practice days, including the traditional Masters Par-3 contest on Wednesday, ahead of wall-to-wall tournament coverage getting under way on Thursday at 2pm.

Featured Group action and updates from around the course are available to enjoy on Sky Sports Golf until the global broadcast window brings full live coverage from 6pm over the first two days, with that available from the earlier time of 5pm for Sunday's final round.

There will be lots of extra action to enjoy on Sky Sports+, with plenty of bonus feeds - including Featured Holes and Featured Groups - allowing you to follow players' progress through various parts of Augusta's famous layout.

Sky Sports subscribers can download the Sky Sports App for free to watch The Masters on their phones, with the website and app also offering news, highlights, latest scores and a live text blog throughout the week.

What time does coverage start of The Masters?

All on Sky Sports Golf and in UK times; timings of the extra feeds are subject to change, based on tee times

Sunday April 12

0900-1100 - Masters Breakfast

1630-0030 - The Masters: Final round LIVE!

1645-2300 - The Masters: Featured Holes/Amen Corner (on Sky Sports+)

*Also on Sky Sports+: On the Range from 1500, Holes from 4,5,6 feed from approx 1530, Featured Groups from approx 1515, Amen Corner from approx 1645, Holes 15+16 feed from 1730

How to watch The Masters in the UK and Ireland

Got Sky?

TV: Sky Customers can watch on Sky Sports Golf, with coverage available at various points throughout the week on Sky Sports Main Event.

App: Sky Customers can also watch on the Sky Sports app

Not got Sky?

Stream: Non-Sky Customers can stream the action with no contract with a NOW Day or a cancel-anytime Month pass

Live blog: Anyone on the move can follow live coverage of The Masters in a dedicated live blog throughout the week.

FREE Highlights: Watch near-live clips and post-round highlights on the Sky Sports app

How to watch The Masters on mobile with the Sky Sports app

Sky Sports Subscribers can:

  1. Download or open the Sky Sports app
  2. Head to the 'Watch' section
  3. Tap on the Sky Sports Golf channel
  4. Sign in with your Sky iD (*you'll only need to do this once)

*Sky iD help: How to find or create your Sky iD

What additional coverage of The Masters is there?

The notorious Amen Corner feed focuses on the famous three-hole stretch from the 11th, while a feed of the fourth, fifth and sixth holes will go live each day as soon as the opening group reach that part of the course and another stream covers the 15th and 16th holes.

The On the Range show covers the practice facility at Augusta National, offering news, analysis, interviews and more, while the Featured Groups feed has four groups a day - two early and two late - and offers each shot of the players selected.

A new documentary reflects on McIlroy's Grand Slam glory last year and another celebrates the 30th anniversary of Sir Nick Faldo's final major success, with an extra programme marking 40 years since Jack Nicklaus won the last of his 18 major titles.

There will be daily highlights available each morning, along with an extended programme of Paul McGinley and Brandel Chamblee debating the biggest storylines during the tournament.

Jamie Weir will host special episodes of the Sky Sports Golf podcast live from Augusta National, available on Apple Podcasts, Spotify or Spreaker, with Sky Sports News offering updates and interviews.

Watch The Masters exclusively live on Sky Sports Golf. Live coverage continues Sunday from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf, with extra feeds available on Sky Sports+. Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract.
